title: Customer Security Review Process (SOP): Questionnaires, Evidence Requests, and SOC 2 Access
author: Olga Petrov
body:
## Purpose
This SOP defines the standard process for responding to customer/prospect security questionnaires and evidence requests (e.g., SOC 2 report, pen test summary, policies). The goals are:
- Provide accurate, consistent, and approved responses.
- Protect restricted artifacts and prevent over-sharing.
- Hit predictable turnaround times to reduce late-stage sales friction.
- Maintain a reviewable audit trail of what was shared, with whom, and under what terms.

**Confidentiality:** This page is **RESTRICTED**. Do not forward, export, or paste its contents externally. All customer-facing sharing must follow the process below.

## Scope
### In scope
- Security questionnaires (SIG Lite, CAIQ, customer templates)
- RFP security sections and standardized responses
- Evidence requests (SOC 2 reports/bridge letters, pen test summaries, vulnerability management overview, subprocessor list, encryption/SSO/audit logging documentation)
- “Written confirmation” requests (retention, deletion, incident notification approach)

### Out of scope
- Contract redlines and legal negotiations beyond standard language (route to Legal)
- New product/security feature commitments (route to Product + Security Engineering)
- Customer requests for direct access to internal systems, dashboards, or raw logs (generally not supported; escalate)

## Roles & ownership
| Area | Primary owner | Backup | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intake + coordination | Solutions Engineering (deal owner) | Sales AE | Owns customer context and timelines |
| Evidence sharing + SOC 2 process | GRC (Olga Petrov) | Daniel Carter | Gatekeeper for restricted artifacts |
| Technical accuracy (audit logs, retention, deployment boundary) | Security Engineering (Marcus Lin / SMEs) | Kevin Osei | Confirms “what is true today” |
| Approved language / kit alignment | Security & Compliance PM (Naomi Feldman) | Docs lead (Elliot Price) | Ensures consistency across enablement kit |
| Contractual claims, DPA/subprocessor contract requests | Legal (Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes) | Finance/Legal intake | Use the Legal intake process |

### Who is allowed to share what
**Public / customer-facing (OK to share without NDA)**
- Public documentation pages (redwood-docs) and the customer-facing one-pagers/FAQ marked as customer-safe
- High-level product security overview and deployment mode security boundary summaries

**Customer-safe under standard mutual NDA (case-by-case; GRC approval required)**
- SOC 2 Type II report and applicable bridge/coverage letters
- Penetration test executive summary (or approved summary letter)
- Selected policies/procedures (sanitized) where required by customer process

**Never share externally (even under NDA) without CISO + Legal approval**
- Raw vulnerability scan outputs, detailed findings, exploit steps, internal tickets
- Full incident postmortems or internal IR runbooks
- Internal architecture diagrams with sensitive identifiers (hostnames, account IDs, security control gaps)
- Employee personal data, customer lists, vendor pricing, internal audit workpapers

If unsure, treat as **restricted** and escalate to GRC.

## Approved sources of truth
Use these resources in order:
1) **Standard RFP Response Library** (approved boilerplate + Hosted/Dedicated/Private variants)
2) **Enterprise Security FAQ v2** (customer-facing, product-aligned answers)
3) **One-pagers** (audit logging, retention, residency, SSO/RBAC, incident response)
4) **Evidence Pointer Index (internal-only)** for where to find the latest artifacts and version stamps

Do not draft “fresh answers” in email unless necessary; copy from approved sources and cite the relevant page/version.

## Intake process
### Supported intake channels
- **Sales / Solutions Engineering:** primary path; attach the questionnaire or link to customer portal
- **Customer Success (renewals):** same workflow; note renewal date and any contractual obligations
- **Partner-led deals:** route through the partner owner + SE, but evidence sharing rules do not change

### Required intake information (minimum)
Provide the following in the intake request:
- Company name, deal stage (or renewal), region, and deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Due date/time and customer timezone
- Evidence requested (exact list) and format (PDF upload, portal, email)
- NDA status (in place / pending / customer refuses)
- Any “must-have” constraints (data residency, audit logs, incident notice language)

If any of the above is missing, GRC may pause work until clarified.

## Triage & turnaround SLAs
### Standard SLA targets (business days)
| Request type | Target SLA | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Simple question / pointer to existing doc | 1 | Example: “Do you support SAML?” |
| Standard questionnaire using approved library | 3 | Customer template up to ~150 questions |
| Large questionnaire (SIG Lite / >150 questions) | 5 | May require multiple reviewers |
| Evidence request (SOC 2 report, pen test summary) with NDA already executed | 2 | Includes tracking + secure delivery |
| Evidence request with NDA not executed | Paused | GRC provides NDA instructions; clock starts after execution |
| Contract language / security appendix redlines | 5–10 | Legal lead; varies by customer |

### Expedites
Expedites are possible when there is a documented commercial impact (e.g., procurement deadline). SE/AEs must:
- State the business justification
- Confirm the customer has granted portal access or email recipient list
- Confirm NDA status

GRC will either approve, propose a partial response, or set an alternate deadline.

## NDA and SOC 2 access flow
### Decision tree
1) **Is there a fully executed NDA covering “confidential audit reports”?**
   - Yes → proceed with evidence sharing.
   - No → do not share SOC 2 or restricted artifacts. Provide the NDA requirement and offer alternative customer-safe summaries.

2) **Is the requester an approved customer recipient?**
   - Must be a legitimate business email for the customer/prospect.
   - Distribution lists are allowed only if the customer confirms membership and responsibility.

3) **Is the artifact in scope for the request and current?**
   - Confirm the artifact version + period of coverage in the Evidence Pointer Index.

### SOC 2 sharing steps (required)
1) **Validate NDA:** confirm execution status in the deal record or with Legal (if unclear).
2) **Confirm scope:** SOC 2 Type II scope and period must be explained accurately (no extrapolation).
3) **Deliver via approved method:**
   - Preferred: secure link in approved drive location with restricted sharing to named recipients
   - Alternate: encrypted email attachment only if secure link is not feasible (coordinate with IT/SecOps if needed)
4) **Log distribution:** record who received which artifact, on what date, and for what opportunity.
5) **Expiration / revocation:** if the deal closes-lost or access must be revoked, remove external sharing permissions.

### Approved external phrasing (SOC 2)
Use approved kit language. Do not state or imply:
- “SOC 2 covers all products/services” (scope matters)
- “Continuous compliance”
- Any guarantee beyond the report

If a customer asks “Are you SOC 2 certified?” respond with the approved phrasing: Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type II audits and can share the report under NDA, including the scope and audit period.

## Evidence package: what we typically share
### Common artifacts (vary by customer)
- SOC 2 Type II report (under NDA)
- SOC 2 bridge/coverage letter if applicable (under NDA)
- Pen test executive summary or approved summary letter (under NDA)
- Subprocessor list (customer-safe; contract/legal may provide canonical list)
- Security FAQ v2 (customer-safe)
- One-pagers (customer-safe)

### If the customer requests “policies”
We generally provide **sanitized policy summaries** rather than full internal policies unless required. Route to GRC for selection and review.

## Questionnaire response workflow
### Step-by-step
1) **Create a tracking record** (system of record depends on deal type):
   - Sales-led: attach questionnaire and status in CRM deal/company record and/or intake ticket
   - Customer renewals: link to renewal record and CSM request
2) **Classify the questionnaire**:
   - Standard (can be answered from RFP library)
   - Requires technical SME input (audit logging details, Private boundary)
   - Requires Legal (DPA, subprocessor contract, security appendix redlines)
3) **Draft responses using approved language**:
   - Copy/paste from the Standard RFP Response Library where possible
   - Use Hosted/Dedicated/Private variants carefully; do not blend responsibility boundaries
4) **SME review (as needed)**:
   - Audit logging/retention: Kevin Osei
   - Deployment boundary (Private/VPC/on-prem): Colin O'Donnell / Vivek Kulkarni
   - Auth/SSO/RBAC: Ethan Park / Kaitlyn Nguyen
5) **GRC final pass**:
   - Verify claims are supportable and consistent with SOC 2 scope
   - Ensure no restricted internal details are included
6) **Send to customer via SE/AE** (unless GRC needs to deliver restricted artifacts directly)
7) **Update tracking** with date sent, version, and any caveats communicated.

### Required response hygiene
- Avoid absolute language (“always,” “never,” “guaranteed,” “impossible”).
- If the answer differs by deployment mode, explicitly separate sections:
  - Hosted
  - Dedicated
  - Private
- For roadmap items: do not commit timelines; use approved “planned/under consideration” wording with disclaimers.

## Escalation paths
Escalate immediately if any of the following occurs:
- Customer asks for “full pen test report,” raw findings, or vulnerability scan data
- Customer requests contractual incident notification timelines in the questionnaire (route to Legal + GRC)
- Customer requests custom security language that contradicts our standard positions
- Customer requests attestations outside our program (e.g., ISO certificate if not available)
- Customer indicates a regulator/auditor will receive the artifacts

### Who to escalate to
- **GRC escalation:** Olga Petrov (primary) / Daniel Carter (backup)
- **Security Engineering:** Marcus Lin (control validation)
- **Security PM:** Naomi Feldman (approved language / enablement alignment)
- **Legal:** Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes (contract language)
- **Executive:** Dr. Aisha Rahman (CISO) for exceptions/high-risk disclosures

Include: customer name, due date, exact request, and what you propose to share.

## Exceptions and approvals
Any exception to evidence sharing rules requires:
- Written approval from **GRC + Legal**, and
- If sensitive security detail is involved, approval from **CISO**

All exceptions must be logged in the tracking record with:
- Artifact(s) shared
- Recipients
- Rationale
- Approvers
- Date shared

## Recordkeeping & audit trail
### What must be recorded
- Customer/prospect name and opportunity/renewal identifier
- NDA status and effective date
- Artifacts shared (exact filenames/versions) and distribution method
- Recipient list
- Date shared and who approved

### Retention
Maintain distribution records for at least the duration required by GRC policy and operational needs. Do not store customer-uploaded questionnaires in personal drives.

## Customer communications guidelines
### What SE/AEs should say when routing to GRC
Use a simple, consistent message:
- We can provide SOC 2 and certain security artifacts under NDA.
- Please confirm recipient emails and upload method.
- We will respond within the stated SLA.

### What not to say
- Do not promise immediate turnaround if NDA is missing.
- Do not “interpret” SOC 2 scope beyond the report.
- Do not provide ad hoc incident notification guarantees; reference the approved one-pager and route contract language to Legal.

## Frequently encountered scenarios
### 1) Customer refuses NDA but requests SOC 2
Response:
- Provide customer-safe one-pagers/FAQ and explain SOC 2 report requires an executed NDA.
- Offer a live walkthrough call where we discuss controls at a high level (no restricted artifact sharing).

### 2) Customer asks: “Do you log prompts/outputs?”
Response:
- Use the approved Audit Logging and Retention one-pagers and specify differences by deployment mode.
- If the customer requests confirmation of their exact configuration, route to SE + Security Eng.

### 3) Customer asks for breach notification “within X hours”
Response:
- Share the Incident Response & Notification one-pager and state that contractual timelines (if any) are governed by the agreement.
- Route requested language to Legal intake.

## Change management
- Owner: **GRC**
- Review cadence: **Quarterly**, and additionally upon:
  - SOC 2 report refresh
  - Major changes to evidence artifacts or security program
  - Material product changes impacting security boundary (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

To request changes: comment on this page and open an internal intake ticket to GRC with the proposed update and justification.

## Appendix: Quick checklist
- [ ] Confirm deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- [ ] Confirm due date/timezone
- [ ] Confirm NDA executed (required for SOC 2 / restricted artifacts)
- [ ] Use approved RFP library language; avoid absolutes
- [ ] Route Legal items (DPA/subprocessors/contractual SLAs) via Legal intake
- [ ] Log what was shared + recipients + date + approvers
- [ ] Revoke access if required
